## Santa Cruz de la Sierra: city life, culture and nature in eastern Bolivia

**Santa Cruz de la Sierra lies in eastern [Bolivia](/bolivia/) and differs from the highland cities of the Altiplano in its warm climate and green urban landscape.** Here you can discover local cuisine, architecture in the historic center and modern neighborhoods before traveling to the region's natural and archaeological sites.

For many travelers, Santa Cruz is their starting point in Bolivia. The city is connected to the transport network in the east of the country, and its location makes it possible to plan a route from tropical and foothill landscapes towards the Andes.

## The historic center: Plaza 24 de Septiembre

The city's main square is **Plaza 24 de Septiembre**. The cathedral, historic buildings, public spaces and cafes surround it. Its name recalls events in the local struggle for independence in 1810.

**San Lorenzo Cathedral**, with its two brick towers, is among the city's most recognizable landmarks. The municipal tourism portal notes that the present structure was built and rebuilt during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Its architecture combines neoclassical features with earlier religious traditions of the city.

Look for the exposed brickwork of the facade, the tall towers and the interior spaces. Visits to the cathedral and its museum area are possible in various formats, but opening hours and access to viewpoints should be confirmed separately.

The historic **Casco Viejo** district covers several streets around the square. Houses with interior galleries, churches, cultural institutions and buildings from different architectural periods survive here.

## What else to see in the city

Santa Cruz is suited to a relaxed city walk before nature excursions. Beyond the historic center, handicraft markets, cafes serving local food and museums are worth exploring. The municipal tourism portal highlights history and art museums and cultural spaces around the old center.

| Experience | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Plaza 24 de Septiembre | Urban history |
| San Lorenzo Cathedral | Religious architecture |
| Casco Viejo | Old neighborhoods and museums |
| Local markets | Crafts and everyday life |

On a city tour, combining historic landmarks with markets lets you experience contemporary Santa Cruz as well as its architecture. Depending on your interests, you can devote more time to art, food or the history of the region.

## From Santa Cruz to Samaipata

One rewarding excursion from the city goes to [Samaipata](/bolivia/place/samaipata/). The mountain region is known for the El Fuerte de Samaipata archaeological complex and the transitional landscapes between the plains and the Andes.

The archaeological site is associated with pre-Columbian cultures and the later history of the Incas. Channels, depressions and other traces of ancient structures can be seen on the rock-carved surface. An expert guide can help explain the site's functions without relying on legends or invented stories.

The trip to Samaipata takes considerable time and is best treated as a full excursion day. On our [12-day Ada Tours journey](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/), an overnight visit to Samaipata follows the introduction to Santa Cruz.

## Nature in Amboró National Park

To the northwest of Santa Cruz lies [Amboró National Park](/bolivia/place/amboro-national-park/). It encompasses a range of forest landscapes, including foothill and humid ecosystems.

Areas of **cloud forest**, with large ferns, mosses and dense vegetation, are especially interesting to visitors. However, the park covers a vast area, and not all sections can be reached by the same road or explored in a short walk.

On the [“Treasures of Bolivia” tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/), Amboró has a dedicated day, with a stop at Cuevas Waterfalls along the way. It illustrates how a nature excursion can be combined with accommodation in Santa Cruz.

A professional nature guide is valuable for bird and wildlife watching. Sightings of rare species cannot be guaranteed.

## Jesuit heritage in the Chiquitos region

Eastern Bolivia is known for the **Jesuit Missions of Chiquitos**. Six historic mission complexes were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1990. Their churches and settlements combine European religious forms with local architecture and craft traditions.

These missions are **not located in downtown Santa Cruz**, so exploring Chiquitos requires separate time and suitable transport. A city walk can introduce the region's historical context, but visiting one city cathedral is not the same as exploring the missions themselves.

This area suits travelers who want to complement a nature itinerary with an exploration of eastern Bolivia's cultural heritage.

## Santa Cruz in Ada Tours itineraries

Santa Cruz appears in several of our current journeys.

The [12-day guided Bolivia tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) begins in Santa Cruz, then visits Samaipata, Amboró National Park, [Sucre](/bolivia/place/sucre/), Potosí and the [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) salt flats. It suits travelers who want to experience the transition from the green east to high-altitude landscapes.

Santa Cruz is also on the [11-day “Titicaca, La Paz, Uyuni and Torotoro” journey](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/). The opening part includes a city sightseeing excursion featuring San Lorenzo Basilica, crafts and a market.

When comparing tours, check how many days are spent in eastern Bolivia, whether Amboró has its own excursion and the order of domestic flights. A ready-made Bolivian itinerary may use Santa Cruz as both a transit and cultural center without including every natural attraction in the surrounding region.

## Frequently asked questions about Santa Cruz

### What should I see in one day?

The historic **Plaza 24 de Septiembre**, San Lorenzo Cathedral, the streets of Casco Viejo and local craft spaces.

### Can I visit Samaipata from Santa Cruz?

Yes. [Samaipata](/bolivia/place/samaipata/) is a separate outing from the Santa Cruz region, and enough time should be allowed for travel and the archaeological complex.

### Are Santa Cruz and La Paz similar?

They are set in different natural environments. Santa Cruz is a warm, low-lying city in the east, while La Paz is in the high Andes. Their climates and acclimatization requirements differ considerably.

### Is Santa Cruz included in Ada Tours sightseeing journeys?

Yes. The city appears on our [12-day](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) and [11-day](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) itineraries, with different onward excursions.

## Santa Cruz on the 11-day journey

The [“Bolivia in 11 Days” itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) starts with arrival in Santa Cruz, an airport welcome and accommodation. The following day is dedicated to city sightseeing. The itinerary names San Lorenzo Basilica, crafts by local makers at Campo Arte, El Abasto market, historic monuments and residential neighborhoods. Travelers get to experience city life before continuing to higher-altitude regions.

For this city day, private transport, admission tickets and guiding in English, Spanish and Russian are explicitly listed. An important detail: **the guide languages are specified for that particular day** and must not automatically be assumed for the entire itinerary.

The route then leads to [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the [Uyuni salt flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and high-altitude lagoons. [Torotoro National Park](/bolivia/place/torotoro/) also features in the program. The result is a journey across several of Bolivia's natural and cultural regions, with Santa Cruz as a meaningful but relatively brief first stop.

This option suits travelers who want to begin with city sightseeing and then focus on the Andes and salt flats. Those particularly interested in eastern Bolivia's heritage and forests should also compare the other tour.

## “Treasures of Bolivia”: Santa Cruz, Samaipata and Amboró

The [12-day “Treasures of Bolivia” tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) spends more time in the east. Day 1 already includes sightseeing in Santa Cruz after the airport welcome and check-in: San Lorenzo Basilica, craft workshops, a market and central neighborhoods.

On the following day, the route continues to [Samaipata](/bolivia/place/samaipata/). The El Fuerte archaeological site here is on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Rock carvings and traces of a ceremonial center reveal the region's cultural history long before modern Santa Cruz.

Day 3 is devoted to [Amboró National Park](/bolivia/place/amboro-national-park/), its cloud forests and a stop at Cuevas Waterfalls on the way back. Travelers then return to Santa Cruz before flying to [Sucre](/bolivia/place/sucre/) on the next stage. The journey continues through [Potosí](/bolivia/place/potosi/), Uyuni, colorful lagoons and Titicaca.

This sequence suits those seeking a combination of colonial cities, archaeology, forests and high-altitude scenery. Eastern Bolivia becomes a distinct section of the trip. The wider coverage means accepting several changes of base and transport stages.

## What really differs between the routes

On the 11-day itinerary, the journey moves on to La Paz, Titicaca, Uyuni and other areas after a dedicated city sightseeing day. The 12-day itinerary first adds Samaipata and Amboró, followed by a flight to Sucre.

| Criterion | What to compare |
|---|---|
| Santa Cruz itself | A full or partial sightseeing day |
| Nature in the east | Whether Samaipata and Amboró are included |
| Onward journey into the Andes | Flights and road transfers |
| Guiding | Guide language on the relevant section |

**One extra day on the overall tour** does not necessarily mean more free time in the city. Check where the dedicated excursions occur, how transfers are arranged and how much time is left to rest after arrival.

If Santa Cruz is only one possible stop, compare [all current Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/). For trips with archaeological sites and historic cities, browse [Bolivia culture and history tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/bolivia/). These selections cover more programs than the catalog of routes via Santa Cruz.

## What to confirm before booking

**Arrival.** Confirm the airport, meeting time and first transfer arrangements. Both itineraries include a welcome in Santa Cruz, but the following sightseeing days differ. A transfer does not mean that international airfare is included.

**Domestic flights.** “Treasures of Bolivia” lists a Santa Cruz–Sucre flight after the eastern section. Check separately whether that flight ticket is included in the chosen price: the travel plan and the services paid for are not the same thing.

**Altitude and exertion.** The high-altitude section begins after eastern Bolivia. Compare overnight elevations, travel days and the transition towards Uyuni and Titicaca. If altitude poses personal health concerns, discuss them with a doctor before departure.

**Clothing.** You will need different gear for city walks, Amboró's humid forests and the dry highlands. Pack for the complete itinerary rather than the weather at your arrival airport alone.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Amboró National Park included on every tour via Santa Cruz?

No. [“Treasures of Bolivia”](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) includes a day in the Amboró area, whereas the [11-day itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) goes on to other regions after the city. Mentioning Santa Cruz does not confirm a park visit.

### Is there a program including Santa Cruz, Sucre and Potosí?

Yes. All three cities are included in the [12-day tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/). The stops differ in their format: some involve sightseeing, others a transfer or a dedicated day of exploring.

### Which tour is best for seeing Santa Cruz itself?

If time in the city streets and market matters, compare the sightseeing days rather than the overall holiday length. The 11-day itinerary has its city tour after the day of arrival; on the 12-day tour, it comes on day 1 before excursions to the surrounding area.

### Where can I find itineraries that do not require a visit to Santa Cruz?

Use the [Bolivia tour catalog](/bolivia/tour/) or the selection of itineraries visiting [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/tour/). Santa Cruz is not a compulsory destination on every journey through the country.

## The Siloli Desert: sculpted rocks among Bolivia's mountains

The Siloli Desert lies in southwestern Bolivia, in the high-altitude region of Sud Lípez. Its landscapes consist of open sandy expanses, rocky ground and mountains. The power of the wind is particularly visible here: individual rock formations have acquired unusual shapes through prolonged erosion.

Siloli is included in extended four-wheel-drive routes between the [Uyuni salt flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and the lakes of the Altiplano. It is neither a sandy resort nor a place for an independent stroll without appropriate transport. The high altitude, cold air and distance from towns shape how visitors must travel.

## The Stone Tree: a symbol of the desert

The **Stone Tree** (Árbol de Piedra) is a rock formation resembling a tree, with a relatively narrow base and a broader top. Its outline was formed by the erosive action of wind and sand. It is one of the Siloli landscape's most recognizable landmarks.

Photograph the rock from the permitted distance. Do not touch or climb fragile stone surfaces or alter the surroundings for a picture. Blowing sand can damage cameras in strong winds; protective equipment and tightly fitting clothing are useful.

## How Siloli differs from other natural areas

At [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the main attractions are the colors of the water, minerals and birds. Around [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), visitors can observe steam vents and hot mud. Siloli is different: its terrain, rock colors, wind and individual unusual formations take center stage.

All these sites belong to the southwestern Altiplano, but they are not a single walkable attraction. Stops on a tour may be spread across different days and depend on the condition of unpaved roads.

| Place | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Siloli | Rocks and desert |
| Stone Tree | Wind erosion |
| Laguna Colorada | High-altitude lake |
| Sol de Mañana | Fumaroles |

## Weather and altitude

Strong winds and sudden cold are possible on the desert plateau. Even in bright sunshine, a windproof jacket, warm layers and a hat may be necessary. The altitude increases physical demands, so travel through southern Bolivia should be planned with acclimatization in mind.

Choose a reliable vehicle, sufficient drinking water and an organized route. Communications and infrastructure are limited in remote areas. Agree on longer stops in advance so the group can reach its next accommodation as planned.

## Can you reach Siloli from Uyuni in one day?

Routes from Uyuni to the southern lagoons follow high-altitude roads and often take several days. Travel time depends on the route, road conditions and number of stops. To experience Siloli properly, include it in a regional expedition rather than planning a short out-and-back trip.

When comparing [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/), look at the duration of the off-road section, overnight altitudes, included meals and transport. Not every Uyuni itinerary visits the Siloli Desert and the Stone Tree.

## Frequently asked questions about the Siloli Desert

### Where is the Siloli Desert?

In southwestern Bolivia, in the high-altitude Sud Lípez region of Potosí Department.

### What is the Stone Tree?

It is a rock formation resembling a tree, sculpted over time by wind erosion.

### Can I travel there independently without a four-wheel-drive vehicle?

The roads and remoteness make ordinary independent travel difficult. Routes through this area generally use suitably equipped vehicles and local guides.

### Are Siloli and the Uyuni salt flats the same place?

No. They are different natural areas of southwestern Bolivia that can be visited on the same longer expedition.

## Which tours pass through the Siloli Desert?

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} whose main routes include the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/). This dry high-altitude region of southwestern Bolivia is known for open rocky terrain and unusual rock formations. One of its most recognizable stops is the [Stone Tree](/bolivia/place/arbol-de-piedra/), a natural formation resembling a trunk and crown.

Siloli is rarely the only destination on a trip. Travelers generally combine it with [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the [Sol de Mañana geothermal field](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), other Altiplano lakes and the [Uyuni salt flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The [Siloli destination page](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) describes the area itself; here the focus is on **comparing the actual itineraries that pass through it**.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_solonchak_uyuni,tour_source_prirodnye_chudesa_bolivii,tour_source_priklyucheniya_v_bolivii,tour_source_sokrovishcha_bolivii,tour_source_velikij_tur_po_yuzhnoj_amerike,tour_peru_bolivia_uyuni_lakes_15_days,tour_south_america_luxury_33_days}}

## A short jeep tour or a longer journey: what to choose?

| Program | Role of Siloli |
|---|---|
| [Uyuni, 3 days](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/) | Day 2, between lagoons and Uyuni |
| [Bolivia, 10 days](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/) | High-altitude stage with an overnight stay |
| [Bolivia, 11 days](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) | Day featuring Stone Tree and lagoons |
| [Peru and Bolivia, 15 days](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) | Day 11, part of a reserve route |
| [VIP South America, 33 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) | Day 17, before crossing into Chile |

**The shortest option** is the [three-day group jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/). It starts at the Hito Cajones border crossing with Chile. Day 1 visits [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the [Salvador Dalí Desert](/bolivia/place/salvador-dali-desert/), [Polques Hot Springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/), Sol de Mañana and Laguna Colorada. On day 2, the vehicle travels via [Laguna Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/), [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), [Laguna Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/) and the Siloli Desert to the Stone Tree. The journey then continues towards Uyuni.

Choose this tour when you want to see the high-altitude lagoons and salt flats in a few busy days. A **group format** is specified. The route does not start in central Uyuni, so the meeting point and border crossing arrangements are especially important.

## For a longer stay in the Siloli area

The [ten-day “Natural Wonders of Bolivia” tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/) explores the southwest in more depth. On day 3 the route travels from the Tahua area past volcanoes towards Siloli, with photography stops and an overnight stay. Day 4 begins early, with the Stone Tree, geothermal vents at Sol de Mañana, hot springs and colorful lagoons following one another.

The key practical difference from the short jeep tour is that the ten-day program includes an overnight stay in Siloli. The itinerary names the Tayka del Desierto hotel, private 4×4 transport, a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking guide, meals and admission tickets as specified in the program. Those conditions apply to this particular trip and must not be assumed for every tour through the desert.

After the Altiplano, the journey continues into another natural region, towards [Rurrenabaque](/bolivia/place/rurrenabaque/), [Madidi National Park](/bolivia/place/madidi-national-park/) and then Titicaca. For travelers wanting to combine dry highlands with tropical rainforest, this variety matters more than simply adding days at the salt flats.

The [11-day Bolivia tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) passes through Siloli during its colorful lagoons and Uyuni stage. The desert is combined with the Stone Tree, Colorada, Sol de Mañana and Polques. Other days feature [Santa Cruz](/bolivia/place/santa-cruz/), Tiwanaku, Titicaca, La Paz and Torotoro. This tour suits people interested in both natural landscapes and cultural stops.

## Siloli on trips through Peru, Bolivia and Chile

The [15-day “Peru and Bolivia: Uyuni and the Altiplano Lakes” tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) visits the desert on day 11. The morning drive passes through Siloli, the Stone Tree and [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). The day's natural attractions also include Laguna Colorada, Sol de Mañana, Polques Hot Springs and Laguna Verde. Before the Bolivia section, the journey visits [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Titicaca.

The [14-day grand tour of Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) also includes Siloli among its high-altitude natural stops. It suits those seeking Bolivian landscapes together with neighboring countries rather than devoting their entire holiday to Bolivia.

On the [33-day VIP South America itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/), Siloli and nearby lagoons appear on day 17, on the way to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The longer format includes many other regions of the continent. The VIP label does not guarantee separate accommodation in the desert or special arrangements at a natural stop: check the exact transport, hotels and guiding in the itinerary.

If Bolivia itself is your priority, explore [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/); for a combination of countries, see [multi-country journeys](/multi-country/). The decision should be based on time in each region, not simply the number of place names in the description.

## What to see in Siloli and nearby

The [Stone Tree](/bolivia/place/arbol-de-piedra/) is a notable landmark for visitors interested in geology and unusual weathered rock formations. The rocks stand amid an open, austere landscape. Other stops reveal a different side of the highlands: reddish [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) is known for flamingos, while [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) has steam vents and hot mud.

These attractions **are not a single walkable site**. Itineraries spread them across road sections between lakes and plateaus. Therefore, a long list of attractions in one day mainly indicates a busy driving schedule. For more time at each stop, study the daily program and departure time.

The area is associated with protected landscapes of southwestern Bolivia, including [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). Entry rules and the current reserve fee should be checked for the specific route. Do not assume admission is included in every published tour price.

## Preparing for a journey through Siloli

**Altitude and cold.** The desert lies in a high-altitude area where wind, dry air and fluctuating temperatures are more noticeable than in lowland cities. Pack warm clothes and sun protection even if your starting point is warm. Discuss altitude-related health concerns with a doctor before traveling.

**Transport.** The confirmed itineraries use four-wheel-drive vehicles for their high-altitude sections. Roads and stops differ from an ordinary city tour: expect lengthy drives. Do not assume you will walk around every attraction simply because they are listed together.

**Accommodation.** The ten-day itinerary explicitly includes an overnight stay in the Siloli area. Other tours may pass through during a single driving day. The hotel, room type and meals depend on the particular program.

**Start and finish.** The Hito Cajones border crossing matters for the three-day jeep tour, while longer Bolivian and multi-country routes begin and end in other cities. Compare logistics leading to the first high-altitude stop as well as the number of days.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I visit the Siloli Desert on a three-day tour?

Yes. The [three-day Uyuni group jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/) includes Siloli and the Stone Tree on day 2 together with high-altitude lagoons. It is a full itinerary with several nature stops.

### Is there a tour with an overnight stay near the desert?

Yes. The [ten-day “Natural Wonders of Bolivia”](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/) itinerary explicitly includes an overnight stay in the Siloli area. This condition applies to this program, not every tour in the catalog.

### Are Siloli and the Uyuni salt flats the same place?

No. The [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) is known for rocky terrain and erosion-sculpted formations, while [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is a salt flat. Most of the programs compared here connect them by road, but they are distinct stops.

### Which tour should I choose for lagoons, geysers and the Stone Tree?

Compare the order of days in itineraries passing through Siloli and the stops around [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), [Polques Hot Springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/) and [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/). A three-day route suits a short journey; programs of 10–12 days or longer provide a broader introduction to Bolivia.

## Sol de Mañana: a geothermal field in Bolivia

Sol de Mañana is a geothermal area in southwestern Bolivia, high on the Altiplano. Steam rises from fissures and openings in the ground, while hot mud bubbles in some spots. From a distance the landscape looks almost otherworldly: minerals color the surface, clouds of steam rise above rocky ground and dry mountains stand around it.

The name “Sol de Mañana geysers” is common in tourist itineraries. Yet the main attractions here are **fumaroles and bubbling mud pools**, not necessarily tall, regular jets of water. Expect the geothermal activity actually present at the specific site rather than an effect the itinerary does not promise.

## What can you see in the geothermal field?

Hot water and steam travel through volcanic rock, emerge at the surface and heat muddy areas. Steam appears especially dramatic against cold air. The sight, the smell of sulfurous gases and the sound of bubbling suggest the powerful activity underground.

Because the ground is hot, the accompanying guide determines where observation is safe. Beneath a thin surface crust there may be scalding water or mud. Do not leave an authorized path for a closer photograph, test the temperature with your hand or approach the rim of a mud pool.

## How Sol de Mañana fits into Altiplano journeys

The geothermal field is usually visited as part of an extended four-wheel-drive journey across southwestern Bolivia. The same broad region contains [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), [Polques Hot Springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/), [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) and other high-altitude natural attractions. Whether they all feature on a given journey depends on the route and road conditions.

For travelers starting from [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), Sol de Mañana is not a short city excursion. It forms part of a multiday expedition with long drives, limited infrastructure and considerable temperature fluctuations.

| Site | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Sol de Mañana | Steam and hot mud |
| Polques | Thermal water |
| Laguna Colorada | Lake and birds |

## Altitude, weather and clothing

The geothermal areas are situated at high altitude. Cold winds can be felt even in sunshine, and the exposed plateau offers little shelter from precipitation and gusts. Warm layered clothing, wind protection and sturdy shoes are essential for leaving the vehicle.

Travelers should plan for acclimatization because the route may cross areas substantially higher than familiar city elevations. If your health raises concerns, discuss preparation for such a journey with a doctor beforehand.

## When to photograph the geothermal field

The morning cold can sometimes make steam more visible, but conditions depend on wind, humidity, precipitation and the field's actual activity. No particular hour can guarantee a photograph. Keep a safe distance when shooting, protect equipment from condensation and follow the guide's instructions.

For a wider journey through southwestern Bolivia, compare [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/) by duration, overnight altitude and confirmed stops. “Uyuni” in a tour title does not necessarily mean that it reaches Sol de Mañana.

## Frequently asked questions about Sol de Mañana

### Is Sol de Mañana an active volcano?

It is a geothermal field of fumaroles and mud pools associated with volcanic activity in the region. The tourist visit focuses on steam vents and hot mud.

### Can I get close to the hot mud?

No. The surface can cause burns, and the ground's stability varies. Observe the field only from permitted areas and follow your guide's instructions.

### Is Sol de Mañana close to Uyuni?

Both belong to southwestern Bolivia, but they are far apart on high-altitude roads. A multiday itinerary is usually required.

### Can the geysers be combined with Polques Hot Springs?

Yes. These sites are often combined on regional four-wheel-drive routes. Actual visits depend on the itinerary, road and conditions on the day.
